newsitem.title: GERMANY: Bremer Vulkan receiver doubts takeover.
newsitem.headline: Bremer Vulkan receiver doubts takeover.

text.p: A takeover of bankrupt shipbuilding group Bremer Vulkan Verbund AG is very unlikely, Jobst Wellensiek, the company's receiver, told Reuters on Wednesday, casting doubt on media reports.
Wellensiek said he was extremely sceptical of the Handelsblatt report that Veba AG and Thyssen AG were interested in buying the defunct Bremer Vulkan, to use its losses to reduce their taxes.
Normally, such a takeover would be preceded by weeks of discussions with the receiver, but no one had contacted Wellensiek, he said.
"This public discussion doesn't fit the picture," Wellensiek said.

He added that the newspaper's estimate of 3-4 billion marks ($1.7-$2.3 billion) in losses at Bremer Vulkan was too high. That figure represented claims against the shipbuilder, but the actual losses were reduced to about 2.5 billion marks, he said.
Veba and Thyssen earlier denied the Handelsblatt report.
Ulrich Noelle, finance senator for Bremen, said at the weekend that he was talking to two potential buyers. But Handelsblatt said Noelle had distanced himself from such plans.
